scope: Spoken cues and delivery actions for the hands-on workshop.

slides.title: Hands-on: Three Operator Cases
slides.say: One notebook. Three operator problems. 90 minutes / three short exercises
slides.action: Have slides, Classroom Labs and the Participant Lab Guide ready. Pair participants. Allow breaks outside the 180 teaching minutes.

slides.title: What is agentic AI?
slides.say: An AI agent chooses a tool, reads its result and chooses the next step toward a goal.
slides.action: Ask which part supplies a physical result. Expected: the numerical tool. Ordinary programs can also contain loops.

slides.title: A tool call and an agent workflow
slides.say: A tool call does one job. An agent links jobs using the returned results.
slides.action: Point to the original function-calling and workflow panels. Follow the source link for lecture p.2.

slides.title: Evidence before an answer
slides.say: WikiChat checks claims before writing. Our lab checks numbers before reporting a result.
slides.action: Point to fact checking before Draft. Ask what numerical evidence a grid proposal would need.

slides.title: Voltage: propose, then check
slides.say: L2 calculates and checks proposals. L10B shows saved Llama tool choices.
slides.action: Preview L2 now; run it after setup, L0 and L1. The bar is a reference result, separate from the P3 replay.

slides.title: Clear rules for tool use
slides.say: Set the inputs, allowed tools, limits and stop rules. Python keeps these rules fixed when Llama chooses a step.
slides.action: Ask which task rules must remain fixed when comparing restoration plans.

slides.title: Restoration: define the service goal
slides.say: The goal changes which loads the solver restores. L6 compares two goals.
slides.action: Compare the cyan critical-service segments. The varied tie is 40 kW, another tie stays at 100 kW, and totals include upstream load.

slides.title: Language and decision checks
slides.say: The source example turns written facts into constraints for a solver. In our lab, Llama requests a study. Python checks it. A person reviews it.
slides.action: Explain SMT briefly as logical constraints and MaxSAT as supporting decision-changing conditions. Our lab uses numerical checks and no SMT guarantee.

slides.title: Cyber: good fit can hide bad data
slides.say: L8 tests misleading readings. L9 shows when to return HOLD or a proposal.
slides.action: Ask why a clear explanation cannot establish sensor trust.

slides.title: Four questions about any result
slides.say: Which tool ran? What did it assume? Which limits passed? What should the operator do next?
slides.action: Collect one example of a missing check, then start Colab setup.

slides.title: One notebook for all three cases
slides.say: Open Classroom Labs and save a copy in Drive. Use it throughout.
slides.action: Open Classroom Labs and save a copy. Keep the same notebook open for all three cases.

slides.title: Colab setup
slides.say: Save a copy, connect a CPU and run setup. Wait for Ready, then run L0 and L1.
slides.action: Connect a CPU runtime and run the first setup cell. Wait for Ready. After a reset, rerun setup and the required earlier cells.

slides.title: Input, run, output
slides.say: Find the L heading and run its whole code cell. Read the output below it. After any edit, rerun the cell.
slides.action: Locate input, play button and output. Run the complete named L cell; slide code is often an excerpt.

slides.title: L0: keep the default settings
slides.say: Leave both switches False. Python calculates new results; Llama replies come from saved records. If data are missing, rerun setup.
slides.action: Run L0 with RUN_OPENDSS=False and RUN_LOCAL_LLAMA=False. If the data check fails, rerun setup.

slides.title: L1: does the result match the request?
slides.say: Read binding_pass. Expect True, False, False. Changed inputs or commands need a new check.
slides.action: Run L1. Read binding_pass as True, False, False. Ask what changed in each row.

slides.title: Case 1: voltage support
slides.say: MPC plans ahead. SAC uses a saved learned policy. Check limits first. Among passing options, a smaller score J is better.
slides.action: Locate L2 and identify this synthetic teaching feeder.

slides.title: Two ways to propose settings
slides.say: MPC plans with a model. SAC proposes from learned weights. Both need the same electrical checks.
slides.action: Define MPC as model predictive control and SAC as Soft Actor–Critic. SAC uses saved weights without training again.

slides.title: A tool result changes the next step
slides.say: The first trial fails. Llama requests the fallback. A passing result goes to human review.
slides.action: Point to the failed check between Llama choices. This is the saved P3 MV/LV study; the fixed comparator reaches the same numerical outcome.

slides.title: Two control settings
slides.say: a controls active power. b controls reactive power. Check inverter capacity, voltage and line current.
slides.action: Explain per unit as a value divided by its base. At RATING_FRACTION=0.80, 100% current denotes the reduced allowance.

slides.title: A tool is a callable function
slides.say: Inputs go in. Calculations run. Results come back. L2 calls this Python function directly.
slides.action: Locate lab.voltage_lab on the next slide. Distinguish a direct Python call from a model-selected request.

slides.title: L2: run the default case
slides.say: Run all of L2. It checks the MPC plan and the saved SAC policy. Read feasible, current_step_J and max_allowed_current_pct.
slides.action: Set LOAD_SCALE=1.0 and RATING_FRACTION=0.80. Run all of L2; read feasible, max_allowed_current_pct and current_step_J.

slides.title: L2: voltage and current plots
slides.say: Left: voltages should stay inside the allowed band. Right: current use should stay below 100% of the allowance.
slides.action: Ask a pair to describe one voltage check and one current check. Use the current run’s outputs.

slides.title: L2: both default proposals pass
slides.say: MPC: 73.62% current use, score J about 0.03110. Saved SAC: 51.68% current use, score J about 0.43643.
slides.action: Read feasibility before penalty. Reference J: MPC about 0.03110, SAC about 0.43643.

slides.title: The limit and the calculated result
slides.say: A rule states the limit. A tool checks the proposal against it. Keep both with the result so the operator can review it.
slides.action: Keep the P3 value separate from the fresh L2 exercise. Ask which remaining checks the operator must review.

slides.title: Exercise 1: lower the current allowance
slides.say: In L2, change RATING_FRACTION from 0.80 to 0.75. Predict, then rerun. Compare feasible, current use and score J for both methods. Does this check cover the whole MV/LV network?
slides.action: FOUR MINUTES: predict for 1 minute, edit/run for 2, report for 1. Change only RATING_FRACTION to 0.75; keep LOAD_SCALE=1.0.

slides.title: Exercise 1: both still pass
slides.say: A smaller allowance makes the same current a larger percentage. At 0.75: MPC uses 78.53%, SAC 54.85%. Both pass this test.
slides.action: Debrief: reference current use becomes 78.527895% for MPC and 54.854158% for SAC. Both pass; default coverage is MV only.

slides.title: L2: reset before continuing
slides.say: Restore LOAD_SCALE=1.0 and RATING_FRACTION=0.80. Rerun L2. L3-L5 use a separate saved case called test_01.
slides.action: Restore LOAD_SCALE=1.0 and RATING_FRACTION=0.80, then rerun L2.

slides.title: New calculations and saved replies
slides.say: Python calculates new results. A saved Llama reply keeps its original inputs. Your changed lab input does not change the saved reply.
slides.action: Ask which evidence mode applies to L2 and to the coming L3 replies.

slides.title: L3: inspect saved model choices
slides.say: Run L3. Read the case ID, chosen operations and recorded times. This cell displays old replies. It makes no new model call.
slides.action: Run L3. Read the original test_01 identifier, requested operation and exact public reason.

slides.title: Different words can request the same trial
slides.say: The notebook groups identical tool requests and settings. A vote chooses what to test next. It does not prove that limits pass.
slides.action: Ask what evidence is required before accepting the selected trial for review.

slides.title: L4: check the selected trial
slides.say: Run L4 after L3. Python checks the selected trial for its original case. Compare majority voting with the saved LinUCB selector, which learns which trial to test.
slides.action: Run L4 after L3. Read the table and separate the fixed selection methods from new numerical checks.

slides.title: L4: read the new check
slides.say: Both selectors choose the same trial and pass the new MV check. new_check_passes is the electrical check. Predicted reward is a learned score.
slides.action: Read operation, new_check_passes and current_step_J. Reference penalty is about 0.031082.

slides.title: L5: check model coverage
slides.say: Leave RUN_OPENDSS=False. Run L5 and read the table. The default checks the test_01 MPC plan with the MV model.
slides.action: Keep RUN_OPENDSS=False. Run L5, read optional_mode and the checked model scope.

slides.title: A PASS has a scope
slides.say: This result covers medium-voltage (MV) phases and currents. A full medium- and low-voltage (MV/LV) request needs the wider check or a HOLD.
slides.action: Ask which missing coverage prevents an MV-only pass from supporting a full MV/LV request.

slides.title: Saved voltage case: check SAC first
slides.say: Llama asks to check SAC. The tool finds a current-limit failure.
slides.action: Identify VERIFY_SAC_FIRST and the recorded numerical failure. Replay the full source later in L10B.

slides.title: Saved voltage case: try the MPC fallback
slides.say: Llama requests the existing MPC plan. The electrical tool checks it.
slides.action: Identify USE_MPC_PLAN. Contrast Llama’s requested step with the returned numerical evidence.

slides.title: Saved voltage case: return for review
slides.say: The checks pass. Human review is still pending. A fixed script gets the same final result.
slides.action: Partner recap: one fresh calculation, one saved model choice and one unresolved operator review. Next, restoration.

slides.title: Case 2: restoring service
slides.say: Use the six-node teaching network with one faulted branch. Compare total service with service to critical loads.
slides.action: Locate L6 and keep the faulted branch unavailable.

slides.title: Two service goals
slides.say: One goal gives extra weight to critical loads. The other restores the most total kW. Both use the same network rules.
slides.action: Ask pairs to state the service goal before choosing the preferred plan.

slides.title: L6: solve the restoration problem
slides.say: Run L6. MILP selects whole loads. A separate search checks its priority score. Read served_kw, critical_kw and MILP_matches_exhaustive_check.
slides.action: Run L6 with original capacities 40, 60, 80, 100 and 120 kW. Read served_kw, critical_kw and MILP_matches_exhaustive_check.

slides.title: L6: read both service plots
slides.say: Left: total kW served. Right: critical kW served. Overlapping markers mean the two goals give the same result.
slides.action: Compare both plots at the same capacity. Ask where the service goals differ.

slides.title: L6: the tradeoff at 40 kW
slides.say: Priority goal: 130 kW total, including 90 kW critical. Most-total-kW goal: 140 kW total, including 30 kW critical.
slides.action: Compare 130 total/90 critical with 140 total/30 critical kW. The goals share the same capacities and rules.

slides.title: Restoration checks
slides.say: Check source paths, branch capacity, power balance and the fault. A separate search checks the priority score.
slides.action: Ask which AC, protection and switching-order checks remain outside this formulation.

slides.title: Exercise 2: increase tie capacity
slides.say: Add 180. to CAPACITIES_KW. Keep 40. first. Predict, then rerun L6. Compare total and critical kW at 40 and 180 kW. At which capacity do the two goals give the same result?
slides.action: FOUR MINUTES: predict for 1 minute, edit/run for 2, report for 1. Append 180. to CAPACITIES_KW and keep 40. first.

slides.title: Exercise 2: enough capacity removes this tradeoff
slides.say: At 180 kW, both goals serve 250 kW total and 90 kW critical. The priority goal helps at some limits. It does not improve every case.
slides.action: Debrief: at 180 kW both methods serve 250 total and 90 critical kW. Explain why the constrained-case tradeoff disappears.

slides.title: L7: test an old result after a change
slides.say: Restore the original capacity list and rerun L6. Run L7. It changes the first request from 40 kW to 20 kW.
slides.action: Restore the original capacity list and rerun L6. Run L7; it binds the first 40 kW record.

slides.title: L7: the old evidence no longer matches
slides.say: Original request: True. Changed request: False. HOLD the old recommendation and request a new solve.
slides.action: Read original contract True and changed rating False. Request a fresh constrained solve.

slides.title: New inputs need new evidence
slides.say: An outdated check does not tell us whether the new plan works. Solve again, check again and attach the new result to the new request.
slides.action: Ask which request fields and evidence must be refreshed after a change.

slides.title: The agent keeps the service goal
slides.say: L6 runs Python directly. The operator sets priorities; MILP selects loads. An agent could request the solve and explain its returned tradeoff.
slides.action: Identify the current Python calculation and the proposed coordinating-agent responsibility.

slides.title: Restoration model limits
slides.say: This graph checks active power, not AC voltage or protection. Selected branches do not specify the order of field switching.
slides.action: Name a further study needed before a real operating decision.

slides.title: Saved restoration case: try another plan
slides.say: Llama requests a trial that restores more load and passes the current check.
slides.action: Read SHED_075, served/critical kW and the passing current check. This archive uses a separate feeder catalog; the fraction selects load objects, not percent kW.

slides.title: Saved restoration case: reject a failed trial
slides.say: The next trial exceeds the current limit. Keep the previous passing plan.
slides.action: Keep the previously passed candidate when SHED_065 fails its current check.

slides.title: Saved restoration case: correct the ranking
slides.say: Python corrects the ranking and rechecks the lowest-cost passing plan.
slides.action: Find the wrong language order and numerical guard retaining E03. Contrast this saved feeder case with L6, then move to cyber.

slides.title: Case 3: suspicious readings
slides.say: Use the separate four-bus DC teaching model. Compare the fit to readings with error against known simulation truth.
slides.action: Locate L8. Explain that the known truth is available for offline teaching comparison.

slides.title: What the residual measures
slides.say: Weighted least squares (WLS) fits the readings. Residual J measures the mismatch. The true state is known in this simulation, not in a live control room.
slides.action: Define WLS as weighted least squares. Ask what small residual establishes and what it leaves open.

slides.title: L8: run two data attacks
slides.say: Run L8 with the default scales. Compare one biased reading with a coordinated change across readings.
slides.action: Run the full default L8 cell. The defensive Hc example assumes knowledge of H and access to modeled unprotected channels.

slides.title: L8: read both cyber plots
slides.say: Left: mismatch J and the alarm threshold. Right: error against simulation truth. A quiet alarm can appear alongside a growing state error.
slides.action: Follow the same curve across residual and state-error plots.

slides.title: L8: a coordinated attack escapes the alarm
slides.say: At scale 1, one biased reading gives J=277.50 and an alarm. The coordinated attack gives J=3.92, no alarm, and 0.02678 rad of state error.
slides.action: Compare no residual alarm with nonzero state error at scale one.

slides.title: Exercise 3: test a small bias
slides.say: Add .10 to ATTACK_SCALES. Predict, then rerun L8. At scale 0.10, compare J, the alarm flag and state error. Does no alarm mean the data are correct?
slides.action: FOUR MINUTES: predict for 1 minute, edit/run for 2, report for 1. Add .10 to ATTACK_SCALES and rerun L8.

slides.title: Exercise 3: a small bias can miss the threshold
slides.say: At scale 0.10, J is about 10.14, below the 15.09 alarm threshold. A quiet alarm alone cannot prove that readings are true.
slides.action: Debrief: isolated-bias J about 10.143237 is below the 15.086272 threshold. Alarm=False despite nonzero error; coordinated J stays about 3.920222.

slides.title: L8: reset before recovery
slides.say: Restore the original attack scales and rerun L8. L9 uses a separate fixed recovery case.
slides.action: Restore the original ATTACK_SCALES tuple and rerun L8.

slides.title: L9: one fixed recovery case
slides.say: Compare the same case with and without readings assumed to be trusted. Your L8 scale change does not change this case.
slides.action: Locate L9 and note that its fixed fixture does not follow the changed L8 sweep.

slides.title: Data trust is an assumption
slides.say: This example assumes three extra angle readings are trustworthy. Neither WLS nor Llama authenticates them.
slides.action: Ask who or what would establish the trusted-data premise outside this calculation.

slides.title: L9: HOLD or PROPOSE
slides.say: Run all of L9. Read status first. Then read the proposed injection and the offline violation count.
slides.action: Run all of L9, including its assertions. Read status, u_pu and offline_actual_violations.

slides.title: L9: two outcomes
slides.say: Without trusted replacement readings: HOLD. With assumed trusted readings: PROPOSE, u about 0.121694 p.u., zero offline model violations.
slides.action: Read HOLD without trusted data and PROPOSE with the assumed trusted set. Reference u is about 0.121694 p.u.; offline toy violations are zero.

slides.title: L9: check the correction
slides.say: A quadratic-program (QP) solver finds the smallest allowed injection that meets the branch limits. One flow: predicted 0.17000 p.u., offline actual 0.17046 p.u., limit 0.18000 p.u.
slides.action: Compare predicted and offline flow checks. These use fixed DC sensitivities, rather than a full AC or dynamic model.

slides.title: A proposal depends on its assumptions
slides.say: Assumed trusted data support the estimate. The solver calculates a correction. The operator still reviews data trust, model coverage and missing checks.
slides.action: Ask what must happen if the trust premise cannot be established. Retain HOLD.

slides.title: Saved cyber case: request the allowed tool
slides.say: Llama selects the supplied recovery tool. Python calculates the correction.
slides.action: Separate what the task already permits from what Llama chooses and Python computes.

slides.title: Saved cyber case: keep human review
slides.say: The model check passes. The operator must still review trust and missing checks.
slides.action: Partner recap: why are PASS and PROPOSE different from approved action? Then inspect the complete replays.

slides.title: L10: inspect the five-role workflow
slides.say: Run L10 to see every recorded stage and result. The stages share case facts, proposals and check results. The next slides explain their jobs.
slides.action: Run L10 to inspect the separate archive. The later L11 switch stays False.

slides.title: L10B: replay the three Llama examples
slides.say: Set SCENARIO to voltage, restoration and cyber. Rerun for each. These are saved replies and tool results. No new Llama call runs here.
slides.action: Run L10B for SCENARIO="voltage", then "restoration", then "cyber". Allow about 2 minutes per episode and swap runner/checker roles. Afterward run L11 with RUN_LOCAL_LLAMA=False.

slides.title: L12: practice operator readback
slides.say: Leave L11 disabled, then run L12. Check the wrong ID, the matching ID and equipment_dispatch=False.
slides.action: After L10B and L11, run all of L12. It returns to L4’s selected test_01 voltage trial. Check wrong-ID rejection, simulated acknowledgment and equipment_dispatch=False.

slides.title: L12: approval must match the checked scope
slides.say: Full MV/LV request: HOLD. The MV teaching request allows a simulated readback. A wrong ID fails. This exercise never sends equipment commands.
slides.action: Explain the full-scope HOLD and the MV-only simulated readback. These do not complete the pending review of a separate old record.

slides.title: Our multi-agent design: five roles
slides.say: The roles pass structured results to each other. Llama handles planning and refinement; Python runs the other stages. This is a custom, role-based Python workflow. It is not five independent LLMs. One Llama 3.1:8b model is called with the Planning Agent and LLM Optimizer roles. Awareness, simulation and verification run Python. The default notebook displays saved role traces in L10 and saved selected episodes in L10B; it does not execute a new multi-agent LLM run. The handoff is structured case facts, candidate IDs, tool results and checks, not an invented agent conversation. src/proposal_workflow.py defines CORE_STAGES, run_proposal_case, evaluate and the ranking guard. A final independent recheck precedes MODEL_RECOMMEND. Human acknowledgment remains separate and pending. Hash checks detect changed records but do not authenticate telemetry.
slides.action: Follow the diagram, then identify the tool result and remaining operator decision.

slides.say: Llama asks for less reactive power, then more solar output. Python checks each new trial. This is a custom, role-based Python workflow. It is not five independent LLMs. One Llama 3.1:8b model is called with the Planning Agent and LLM Optimizer roles. Awareness, simulation and verification run Python. The default notebook displays saved role traces in L10 and saved selected episodes in L10B; it does not execute a new multi-agent LLM run. The handoff is structured case facts, candidate IDs, tool results and checks, not an invented agent conversation. src/proposal_workflow.py defines CORE_STAGES, run_proposal_case, evaluate and the ranking guard. A final independent recheck precedes MODEL_RECOMMEND. Human acknowledgment remains separate and pending. Hash checks detect changed records but do not authenticate telemetry. In this L10 lindistflow3 record, the optimizer asks for RELAX_Q_10_PERCENT then INCREASE_PV_0025. Python recalculates each proposal and the verification stage checks it. The selected final recheck uses a=0.3394386941 and b=0.0276310594, with 50.75344954 percent allowed-current use and no recorded violations. The scope is MV phases only with ideal LV aggregation. Do not substitute the P3 99.604410 percent result or L2 MPC score. These are different experiments.

slides.title: Five roles in the restoration case
slides.say: The goal stays fixed. A failed trial cannot enter the final ranking, and Python corrects a wrong cost order. This is a custom, role-based Python workflow. It is not five independent LLMs. One Llama 3.1:8b model is called with the Planning Agent and LLM Optimizer roles. Awareness, simulation and verification run Python. The default notebook displays saved role traces in L10 and saved selected episodes in L10B; it does not execute a new multi-agent LLM run. The handoff is structured case facts, candidate IDs, tool results and checks, not an invented agent conversation. src/proposal_workflow.py defines CORE_STAGES, run_proposal_case, evaluate and the ranking guard. A final independent recheck precedes MODEL_RECOMMEND. Human acknowledgment remains separate and pending. Hash checks detect changed records but do not authenticate telemetry. The L10 lindistflow3 restoration record uses a feeder bypass catalog. SHED_075 returns 1843.61355 kW served and 474.03975 critical kW at 91.86721465 percent allowed-current use. SHED_065 then fails at 111.009413 percent. Llama ranks E02 before E03 even though E03 has the smaller cost. The numerical guard selects E03, then records the final recheck as E05. Switching sequence and broader physical operation are not established.

slides.title: Five roles in the cyber case
slides.say: The workflow keeps the trust assumption visible. It cannot create trusted data from a convincing answer. This is a custom, role-based Python workflow. It is not five independent LLMs. One Llama 3.1:8b model is called with the Planning Agent and LLM Optimizer roles. Awareness, simulation and verification run Python. The default notebook displays saved role traces in L10 and saved selected episodes in L10B; it does not execute a new multi-agent LLM run. The handoff is structured case facts, candidate IDs, tool results and checks, not an invented agent conversation. src/proposal_workflow.py defines CORE_STAGES, run_proposal_case, evaluate and the ranking guard. A final independent recheck precedes MODEL_RECOMMEND. Human acknowledgment remains separate and pending. Hash checks detect changed records but do not authenticate telemetry. Awareness preserves the declared measurement-trust condition. Planning requests the initial candidates; Python runs the estimator and constrained-response tools. The optimizer requests EXTRA_MARGIN_001 and TRUSTED_QP. The selected final recheck uses TRUSTED_QP with u=0.1216936673 per unit and predicted flow12=0.17 per unit against a 0.18 limit. The model checks a four-bus DC fixture with three protected angles assumed trustworthy. No stage authenticates those channels, and offline truth is not fed to Llama.
slides.action: Follow the diagram, then identify the tool result and remaining operator decision.

slides.title: The operator reviews one evidence packet
slides.say: Review the inputs, proposal, worst margins and missing checks. Request another study, reject the proposal or accept it for the next authorized step. Proposed control-room use. The operator reviews the case snapshot, data quality, limits, selected proposal and missing studies. Ask for another study, reject it or accept it for a defined next step. L12 practices ID-bound readback only and never operates equipment.
slides.action: Follow the diagram, then identify the tool result and remaining operator decision.

slides.title: What the evidence shows
slides.say: In L10, five paired final costs tied; one Llama route was worse. Start with past cases and read-only use. Measure benefit against the same tools in a fixed script. The six matched fixed-versus-Llama runs in proposal_complete_workflow.json have five tied final costs and one worse Llama voltage result. Recorded model calls add elapsed time. This demonstrates traceable coordination, not better power-flow solvers or general efficiency. Test any proposed benefit against the same tools and budgets. A control-room pilot starts with archived cases, then read-only shadow studies and a limited reviewed scope.
slides.action: Follow the diagram, then identify the tool result and remaining operator decision.

slides.title: Questions and your next lab run
slides.say: Choose one case. Change one input, rerun and save the result. Explain the agent choice, tool result, check and operator decision. Close by connecting the full loop: a goal, an allowed agent choice, a tool result, a check and a human decision. Ask each learner to name one case and one changed input they can repeat after the session. Save the notebook. Use the source guide for complete references, not as another required activity.
slides.action: Invite questions. Ask learners to save one changed input, result and next decision.
